title: The Volleyball Tournament
summary: A girls' volleyball team that struggles with communication on the court learns to call out plays and support each other, and plays their most coordinated match yet at the school tournament.
poll: Talking to your teammates matters more than individual skill.

versions.title: The Team That Talks
versions.text:
Dana played on the school volleyball team. She was the captain. Her coach was Coach Amal.

The team had a problem. No one called the ball. Two players ran for the same ball. Other balls hit the floor. No one moved.

At practice, Coach Amal stopped the game. She said, "You must talk to each other. Call out 'Mine!' when you want the ball."

The team began to practice this. Dana called, "Mine!" Her teammate Rima called, "Mine!" too. They did not run into each other.

The girls also learned to cheer. When Hind missed a hit, Dana said, "Good try! Get the next one!" Hind smiled and tried again.

Soon the team had a big match. It was the school tournament. Many parents came to watch.

During the match, the girls called out every play. "Mine!" "Switch!" "Nice serve!" They moved together like one team.

It was their best match of the year. They won the game! The team cheered and hugged.

Coach Amal smiled. "You talked to each other," she said. "That is why you played so well."

versions.title: The Team That Talks
versions.text:
Dana played on her school's volleyball team, and she had served as team captain for a full year, trying her best to keep everyone focused and united on the court. Her coach, Coach Amal, had trained the team for two seasons and understood each player's particular strengths and weaknesses.

The team had one persistent, deep-rooted problem that kept costing them valuable points during matches throughout the entire season. No one called out the ball during a play, so communication on the court remained consistently deficient, and this lack of coordination was generating considerable frustration for everyone, including Coach Amal. Sometimes two players ran for the same ball at once and collided painfully and awkwardly in the middle of the court, while other times an easy ball hit the floor because no one bothered to move for it at all.

At practice one afternoon, Coach Amal stopped the game to address her entire team with evident seriousness about this recurring problem. "You must talk to each other constantly on the court," she explained with evident patience. "Call out 'Mine!' whenever you want the ball, so your teammates immediately know not to run for it too, and collisions like these will simply stop happening."

The team began practicing this new habit of calling out plays every single day without exception, and the change in confidence was noticeable almost immediately to any careful observer. Dana called out, "Mine!" and her teammate Rima called out, "Mine!" too, whenever the ball approached her position on the court, and slowly, over several weeks of practice, the painful collisions gradually ceased occurring altogether.

The players also learned to support one another after every single play, whether it went well or poorly for the team, which cultivated genuine, lasting trust between teammates who had once blamed each other for mistakes. When a teammate named Hind missed an easy hit, Dana said, "Good try! Get the next one!" and Hind smiled, feeling encouraged enough to try again immediately rather than dwelling on the mistake.

Soon the team faced its biggest match of the year at the school tournament, a match that would test everything they had practiced together. Many parents and friends filled the gym to watch the girls compete on that important afternoon.

During the match, the girls called out every single play they made throughout the entire game, and their new strategy of constant communication clearly and substantially paid off. "Mine!" "Switch!" "Nice serve!" They moved together across the court with remarkable coordination, functioning almost like a single unit, never once colliding with each other, each player trusting the others completely.

It turned out to be their best match of the entire year, by a wide margin over any previous game they had played together. In the end, the team won the game, and everyone on the court erupted in celebration, cheering loudly and embracing one another with genuine pride in what they had accomplished.

Coach Amal regarded her players with evident pride and satisfaction after the final point was scored. "You talked to each other out there," she said warmly. "That teamwork and clear communication is precisely why you competed with such confidence, coordination, and composure today."

Coach Amal embraced her players with evident pride and satisfaction after the final point was scored. "You communicated with each other so effectively out there," she said warmly, "and that disciplined teamwork and unmistakably clear communication is precisely why you competed with such remarkable confidence, coordination, and composure today, more than at any other point this entire season."
